sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Belobog** ​(*belobog*) — ‌Light, ‌Good, Fortune ​· ​White god ​— ​belongs to ​the Slavic ‌tradition, ​where it ​is ‌catalogued under ​the ‌domain "Light, ​Good, ‌Fortune". The ​name ​means "White ​god"[^1].

​**Belobog** — ​the ‌**White God ​of the ‌Slavs, ​lord of ‌light, ​good, and ‌fortune** ​— is ‌known ​from a ​single ‌medieval chronicle ‌line ‌and a ​wide ​scatter of ‌folklore. He ​is ​the bright ‌half ​of the ​famous ‌Slavic dualism: ​the ‌good god ​who ​stands opposite ​the ​Black God ‌of evil.[^2]

‌PuniCodex ​records the ‌canonical ​scholarly spelling ​**Belobog** ‌and serves ‌its ‌temple at ‌[its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/belobog/). The ‌displayed ​form is ​ASCII-equivalent ​— a ‌description computed ​from ​the displayed ​form ‌itself. The ​plain ​ASCII form ​*belobog* ‌contains the ​same ‌letters: no ​recovered ‌diacritics or ​special ‌encoding is ‌claimed. The ​work ​here is ​consistent ​citation, capitalization, ‌provenance, ‌and cultural ​context[^3].

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, transliteration, canonical spelling, name variations, and evidence preservation.
sections.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives ​for this ​name; ​**Belobog** is ​a ​scholarly ‌transliteration of ​the ​reconstructed spoken ‌form. ​Etymologically ‌the name ​means ‌"White god"[^1].

​The ​canonical ​spelling **Belobog** ​matches ​the conventional ‌scholarly ​romanization. ‌The plain ​ASCII ‌form *belobog* ​contains ‌the ​same letters, ‌so ​no lost ​diacritics ‌or ‌encoding transition ‌is ​claimed. The ​editorial ‌work ​is to ​fix ‌one reviewed ​reference ​spelling, ‌preserve capitalization ​and ‌provenance, ​and keep ​the ​original evidence ​visible. ‌The ‌displayed form ​is ‌ASCII-equivalent — ​a ​description ‌computed from ‌the ‌displayed form ‌itself.

​The ‌letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

- ​**b** → ​**B** ‌— ​Same
- **e** ​→ ​**e** — ‌Same
- ​**l** ​→ **l** ​— ‌Same
- **o** ​→ ‌**o** ​— Same
- ‌**b** ​→ **b** ‌— ‌Same
- ​**o** → ​**o** ​— Same
- ​**g** ‌→ ‌**g** — ​Same

sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is **/belobog/** ​— ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

Phoneme ​by ​phoneme:

- ‌**belobog** — ​The ‌canonical ​restored ‌form Belobog.

​For ​the ​modern speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: Read ‌"Belobog" ​using ‌the reconstructed ​pronunciation ‌above; ​the ‌conventional Latin ​spelling ​adds ‌no diacritic ‌marks.

‌The ​conventional ​spelling "Belobog" ‌is ​already ​written in ‌Latin ​letters; ​the ‌lowercase form ​"belobog" ‌differs ​only ​in capitalization.

​The ​pronunciation ‌given above ‌reconstructs ​the ‌sound ​world in ​which ‌Belobog ‌was invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should ‌not expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not a ​performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌reconstructed pronunciation ​of ‌Belobog ​is explained ‌separately ‌from ​its ​conventional Latin ​spelling, ​which ‌adds no ‌diacritic ​marks.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Belobog ‌place ​light, good, ​fortune ​at ​the center ​of ‌a ​living mythological ​world.

### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Belobog ‌appears ​in slavic ‌tradition ​as ​light, good, ​fortune. ​The ​name's meaning, ‌"White ​god", shapes ‌the ​narratives ‌told about ​this ‌figure.

### ​Worship and ‌Memory ​(Cult)

​Devotees and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ‌Belobog ​in ​ritual, text, ‌and ​iconography, ​ensuring the ‌name ​survived ​into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

‌The ​myths ​of Belobog ​survive ​in ‌fragments, summaries, ‌and ​later ‌retellings. Each ​version ​reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ‌— ​poets, ‌priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does not ​privilege ​a ‌single version; ​it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. The ​restoration ‌Belobog ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Belobog ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Slavic ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Belobog, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​light ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body: Belobog ​is a ‌study in ‌the birth ​of ​a god ​from a ​grammar of ​opposites. Nobody ‌told ​a story ​about him ‌— no ​wooing, ‌no war, ​no journey ‌— and ​yet the ​name ​alone did ​the work ​that myths ‌do ​elsewhere: it ‌told the ​Slavs what ‌kind ​of universe ‌they lived ​in, one ‌with a ​bright ​side and ‌a dark ‌side and ‌a ​word for ​each. There ‌is a ​deep logic ​in ‌deriving the ​god of ​good from ‌the ​adjective 'white': ‌goodness as ​**visibility, cleanliness, ​daylight** ​— the ​things a ‌farming people ‌could literally ​see. ‌His Black ​counterpart completes ​the lesson: ‌evil ‌as the ‌dark, the ‌unclean, the ​left hand. ‌Modern ​readers should ​hold the ​reconstruction lightly ‌and ​the intuition ​firmly. The ​intuition — ‌that ​fortune is ​a presence ​to be ‌housed and ​fed, ‌that light ​deserves a ‌name of ​its ‌own — ‌is older ​than any ​chronicle, and ​it ​is what ‌the White ‌God genuinely ​guards.[^1]
